Silicone Coating Restoration for Aging Winston-Salem Roofs

Silicone coating is a restoration strategy, not a replacement product, and we specify it where an existing roof's membrane or metal surface is sound enough to extend rather than tear off. It's the coating we reach for most often on roofs with standing water, because silicone tolerates ponding in a way acrylic coatings generally don't.

Moisture Survey Before Any Coating Proposal

Coating over wet insulation traps moisture under a sealed surface and accelerates deck deterioration rather than stopping it, so every coating proposal we write starts with a moisture survey, typically infrared scan or core samples, to confirm the substrate is dry before recommending silicone over anything else. If the survey finds meaningful wet insulation, we don't propose a coating; we propose tear-off or targeted insulation replacement first.

A moisture survey also identifies existing membrane defects, splits, open seams, deteriorated flashing, that need repair before coating goes down. Coating seals a sound surface; it doesn't fix an active leak path.

Ponding Water Performance

Standing water is common on older flat roofs across Winston-Salem's institutional and manufacturing building stock, particularly where drainage was marginal at original construction or has degraded as the deck settles over decades. Silicone's tolerance for sustained water contact, without the softening or degradation that affects some acrylic formulations, makes it the coating we specify on roofs where ponding is a documented, ongoing condition rather than an occasional event after heavy rain.

  • Infrared moisture scan or core sampling performed before any coating is proposed
  • Existing membrane defects repaired ahead of coating application
  • Dry film thickness specified in mils and documented at application
  • Substrate compatibility confirmed for EPDM, BUR, modified bitumen, or metal
  • Ponding areas identified and addressed with additional coating thickness where needed
  • Recoat cycle and expected service life extension documented in writing

Substrate Compatibility

Silicone coatings adhere well to EPDM, aged BUR and modified bitumen, and metal roofing, which covers a large share of the older roof stock we're asked to evaluate for a restoration rather than replacement approach around Winston-Salem's manufacturing and institutional buildings. Adhesion testing on a sample area of the existing substrate is part of our process before committing to a full coating scope, since surface contamination or prior coating history can affect how well silicone bonds.

Dry Mil Thickness and Documentation

Coating performance depends directly on applied dry film thickness, and under-application is one of the more common reasons a coating fails to deliver its expected service life extension. We specify target mil thickness in writing and document actual application, since this is the number a manufacturer warranty is typically tied to, not a general description of coats applied.

Reinforcement at Seams and Penetrations

Flat field areas of a coating system generally perform well without reinforcement, but seams, curbs, penetrations, and drain areas see more movement and stress concentration than the open field does, and that's where we typically specify a polyester fabric reinforcement embedded in the coating rather than relying on the coating's tensile strength alone. This adds tear and puncture resistance exactly where the roof's existing weak points already are, rather than treating every square foot of the roof as an equal risk.

Reinforcement is a labor-intensive detail to install correctly, and it's one of the places a lower-cost coating bid tends to cut corners. We document where reinforcement is specified on the roof plan so it's clear in the proposal, not assumed as standard practice everywhere.

When Coating Isn't the Right Answer

We turn down coating scopes where the underlying membrane or deck condition doesn't support it: active leaks not yet repaired, insulation that's already wet, or a roof already past the point where a coating extends service life meaningfully rather than just delaying an inevitable reroof by a year or two. Owners get that assessment in writing, with the moisture survey data behind it, rather than a coating proposal that papers over a problem.

Coordinating Coating Projects on Occupied Buildings

Coating application generates far less disruption than a tear-off or even a recover, since it doesn't involve removing any existing roofing material, which is a large part of why it's attractive on occupied medical office and manufacturing buildings where downtime carries real cost. We still coordinate application scheduling around rooftop equipment access and any exhaust or intake locations nearby, since coating odor during cure, while less disruptive than demolition, is still worth planning around for buildings with sensitive interior operations or fresh-air intake near the roof surface.

Common Questions on Silicone Roof Coatings

Can silicone coating be applied over any existing roof?

Only after a moisture survey confirms the substrate is dry and any membrane defects are repaired first. Coating over wet insulation traps moisture and accelerates deterioration.

Does silicone handle standing water better than acrylic?

Yes, silicone generally tolerates sustained ponding without the softening some acrylic formulations experience, which is why we specify it on roofs with a documented ponding condition.

What roof types can be coated with silicone?

EPDM, aged BUR, modified bitumen, and metal roofing are all common substrates, provided adhesion testing confirms compatibility with the existing surface.

How is coating thickness verified?

We specify a target dry film thickness in mils and document actual applied thickness, since manufacturer warranties are typically tied to that number.

When would you recommend against coating?

When a moisture survey finds wet insulation, when active leaks haven't been repaired, or when the roof is already past the point where coating meaningfully extends service life.
